sentences.text: Holonema was an extinct genus of large, barrel-shaped arthrodire placoderms, a group of armored fish.
While most Holonema species are known only from armor fragments, H. westolli is known from complete, articulated specimens.
The species H. westolli reached a length of approximately 60.6 centimeters.
The median dorsal plate of H. radiatum averages about 30 centimeters in length.
The median dorsal plate of H. haiti is estimated to be about 28 centimeters in length.
The median dorsal plates of H. farrowi range up to 20 centimeters in length.
H. obrutshevi is distinguished by a small, horn-like process on its median dorsal plate.
H. harmae is distinguished by the spinal and subpectoral margins of its anterior-ventral plates meeting at almost a right angle.
H. haiti is known for having a very narrow median dorsal plate compared to other species.
Fossil Holonema individuals contained stones and feldspar pieces in their armor, suggesting they used these as gastroliths to aid digestion.
The genus Holonema was first described by Newberry in 1889.
The type species of the genus Holonema is Pterichthys rugosum.
Researchers believe Holonema was a benthic-dwelling fish due to its cambered body shape.
Recent studies of the jaw and toothplates suggest Holonema likely had a planktivorous lifestyle.
Holonema is classified within the class Placodermi.
Holonema belongs to the family Holonematidae.
Holonema lived from the Emsian to the Famennian, between 399.5 and 358.86 million years ago.
Holonema fossils have been found in oceans worldwide during the Mid to Late Devonian periods.
It is debated whether H. ornatum belongs to the genus Holonema, as Denison (1978) suggested it might not.
